## How to use this page

1. **Read it once** — about 8 minutes.
2. **Mark the 10–12 formulas you find easiest to remember.** Memorize those.
3. **In the room**, pattern-match: read the problem, find the section, find the matching formula, plug in numbers.
4. **The decision rules** at the bottom of each section are the tiebreakers when two formulas could apply. Memorize those verbatim.

---

## 🪙 Bonds

```{=html}
<div class="fb-grid">
  <div class="fb-card fb-bond">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Coupon rate</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Annual coupon $ / Face value</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-bond">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Interest expense (per period)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= NBV at start of period × MARKET rate</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">⚠️ Use MARKET rate, not coupon rate.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-bond">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Amortization (per period)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Coupon paid (cash) − Interest expense</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-bond">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>New NBV (premium bond)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Old NBV − Amortization</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">For discount bonds: Old NBV + Amortization (NBV climbs toward face).</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-bond">
    <div class="fb-tag">JOURNAL ENTRY</div>
    <h4>Issuance (always 3 lines)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">Dr. Cash (issue price) · Cr. Bonds Payable (face) · Cr/Dr. Premium/Discount (the difference)</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-bond">
    <div class="fb-tag">JOURNAL ENTRY</div>
    <h4>Retirement at maturity</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">Dr. Bonds Payable (face) · Cr. Cash (face)</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="fb-rule">
<strong>DECISION RULE — Premium vs Discount:</strong>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Premium</strong>: Issue price &gt; Face · Coupon rate &gt; Market rate · Total interest expense &lt; Total coupons</li>
  <li><strong>Discount</strong>: Issue price &lt; Face · Coupon rate &lt; Market rate · Total interest expense &gt; Total coupons</li>
  <li><strong>Face value</strong>: Issue price = Face · Coupon = Market</li>
</ul>
</div>
```

## 💵 Statement of Cash Flows (Indirect Method)

```{=html}
<div class="fb-grid">
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">RECIPE</div>
    <h4>Cash Flow from Operations</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= NI + non-cash expenses + non-cash losses − non-cash gains ± Δ in current operating accounts</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Cash from sale of PPE</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= NBV − Loss (or NBV + Gain)<br>NBV = Original cost − Accumulated depreciation</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Dividends paid</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Beg RE + NI − End RE</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">From the Retained Earnings roll-forward.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>PPE purchased (cash)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">From PP&amp;E roll: End PPE = Beg PPE + Purchases − Cost of PPE sold</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Cash interest paid</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Interest expense ± Δ in Interest Payable<br>(if no IP balance, = interest expense)</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Tax rate</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Tax expense / Pretax income<br>Pretax income = Operating income − Interest exp − Loss on sale</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Cash Flow from Financing</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= ΔLong-term debt + ΔCommon stock + ΔAdditional paid-in capital − Dividends paid</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-scf">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Reconciliation check</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">CFO + CFI + CFF = ΔCash on Balance Sheet</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="fb-rule">
<strong>SIGN RULE — the most important rule on the SCF:</strong>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Current ASSETS</strong> (AR, Inventory, Prepaid) → <strong>OPPOSITE sign</strong> from the change. AR up = cash use (subtract). AR down = cash source (add).</li>
  <li><strong>Current LIABILITIES</strong> (AP, Accrued, Wages payable) → <strong>SAME sign</strong> as the change. AP up = cash source (add). AP down = cash use (subtract).</li>
  <li><strong>Non-cash items</strong> (depreciation, loss on sale, amortization) → <strong>add back</strong>. Non-cash gains → subtract.</li>
</ul>
</div>
```

## 🏭 Job-Order Costing

```{=html}
<div class="fb-grid">
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Predetermined OH rate</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= ESTIMATED total OH / ESTIMATED allocation base</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">Computed at start of year. Always uses estimates.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Allocated (applied) OH</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Predetermined OH rate × ACTUAL allocation base</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">Predetermined × ACTUAL. Mixed.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Direct materials used</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Materials placed in production − Indirect materials</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">Don't use materials purchased — use materials placed.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Manufacturing OH actually incurred</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Indirect materials + Indirect labor (incl. supervisor) + Factory rent + Factory dep + Factory utilities</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Total product cost</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Direct materials + Direct labor + Allocated OH</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Period costs</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Corporate HQ rent + Office salaries + Customer service + Sales + Marketing + SG&amp;A</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Cost of Goods Manufactured (COGM)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Beg WIP + (DM used + DL + MOH) − End WIP</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-job">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Beg Finished Goods + COGM − End Finished Goods</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="fb-rule">
<strong>DECISION RULE — Product vs Period:</strong>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Product cost</strong> (capitalized into inventory, expensed when sold as COGS): direct materials + direct labor + ALL factory-related overhead. <em>"If it's tied to the factory, it's product."</em></li>
  <li><strong>Period cost</strong> (expensed immediately): corporate HQ, office admin, sales, marketing, customer service. <em>"If it's tied to anything besides the factory, it's period."</em></li>
</ul>

<strong>DECISION RULE — Direct vs Indirect (within product costs):</strong>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Direct material</strong>: traceable to one unit (candy wrappers in candy, fabric in shirts).</li>
  <li><strong>Direct labor</strong>: traceable to one unit (assembly-line worker wages).</li>
  <li><strong>Indirect material</strong>: factory but not per-unit (lubricants, glue, screws). → Goes into MOH.</li>
  <li><strong>Indirect labor</strong>: factory but not per-unit (supervisor, janitor). → Goes into MOH.</li>
</ul>
</div>
```

## 📈 CVP Analysis

```{=html}
<div class="fb-grid">
  <div class="fb-card fb-cvp">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Unit Contribution Margin</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">Unit CM = Sales price/unit − Variable cost/unit</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-cvp">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>CM Ratio</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Unit CM / Sales price/unit<br>OR = Total CM / Total Sales</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-cvp">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Breakeven (units)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Fixed Costs / Unit CM</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">Always round UP — you can't sell partial units.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-cvp">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Breakeven (sales $)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Fixed Costs / CM Ratio</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-cvp">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Units for target profit</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) / Unit CM</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-cvp">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>NI at any volume</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= (Volume × Unit CM) − Fixed Costs</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-cvp">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Variable Expense Ratio (VER)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Variable Costs / Sales = 1 − CM Ratio</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="fb-rule">
<strong>DECISION RULE — Scenario Analysis:</strong>
Every scenario changes one or more of: <strong>(a)</strong> sales price, <strong>(b)</strong> variable cost per unit, <strong>(c)</strong> total fixed costs.

Always do this in order:
<ol>
<li>Recompute the new variable cost per unit.</li>
<li>Recompute the new fixed costs.</li>
<li>Recompute the new unit CM.</li>
<li>Then plug into breakeven / target-profit / NI formulas.</li>
</ol>

Never use stale values from the prior scenario.
</div>
```

## 🧮 Ratios (for MC questions)

```{=html}
<div class="fb-grid">
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Current Ratio (liquidity)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Current Assets / Current Liabilities</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">Higher = more liquid. &gt;1 typically healthy.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>ROA (profitability)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Net Income / Average Total Assets</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Times Interest Earned (solvency)</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= EBIT / Interest Expense<br>OR = (NI + Interest + Tax) / Interest</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">Higher = better at covering interest.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Debt-to-Assets</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Total Debt / Total Assets</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Debt-to-Equity</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Total Debt / Shareholders' Equity</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>P/E Ratio</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Market price per share / EPS</p>
    <p class="fb-warn">Higher = market expects growth (NOT current profitability).</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Dividend Payout Ratio</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Dividends per share / EPS<br>OR = Total Dividends / Net Income</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Inventory Turnover</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= COGS / Average Inventory</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-card fb-ratio">
    <div class="fb-tag">FORMULA</div>
    <h4>Profit Margin</h4>
    <p class="fb-formula">= Net Income / Sales</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## 📊 Income Statement Formats

```{=html}
<div class="fb-comp">
  <div class="fb-comp-side">
    <h4>Contribution Margin Format (internal use)</h4>
    <pre>
Revenue                   ___
− Variable Costs         (___)
= Contribution Margin     ___
− Fixed Costs            (___)
= Operating Income        ___
    </pre>
    <p>Used for break-even, pricing, CVP analysis, internal management.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="fb-comp-side">
    <h4>GAAP Format (external use)</h4>
    <pre>
Revenue                   ___
− COGS                   (___)
= Gross Profit            ___
− Operating Expenses     (___)
= Operating Income        ___
    </pre>
    <p>Required for external financial statements (banks, investors, taxes).</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Memorize check (3 minutes)

If you can do these from memory, you're ready.

```{=html}
<ol class="memo-check">
  <li>Bond interest expense formula: <strong>NBV × MARKET rate</strong>.</li>
  <li>SCF sign rule: current assets opposite, current liabilities same.</li>
  <li>Cash from PPE sale: <strong>NBV − Loss</strong>.</li>
  <li>Dividends paid: <strong>Beg RE + NI − End RE</strong>.</li>
  <li>Predetermined OH rate: <strong>Estimated / Estimated</strong>.</li>
  <li>Allocated OH: <strong>Predetermined × ACTUAL</strong>.</li>
  <li>Breakeven: <strong>FC ÷ unit CM</strong>. Round up.</li>
  <li>Target profit units: <strong>(FC + target) ÷ unit CM</strong>.</li>
  <li>Stock split = SE unchanged. Stock repurchase = SE decreases.</li>
  <li>P/E high = market expects growth.</li>
</ol>
```
